evidence: docker.rs:16-55 derives an absolute canonical configuration-directory reference digest plus DOCKER_HOST presence, without reading configuration/auth contents. Relative and unusable references refuse.

The Grant carries the qualified caller routing. execute recomputes the actual shim routing before command construction/spawn and refuses divergence/host overrides rather than relying on a context name.

Historical cleanup compares the current Runtime routing with the recorded config digest before daemon probes. Engine/context checks remain separate, and changed configuration references do not silently rebind prior target authority.

The new managed_docker.rs actual built-binary/IPC control uses two owned synthetic config roots, same-named default contexts and different synthetic engines; it asserts config/host mismatch refusal before probes/creation plus a matching real shim path/ledger identity. Read, not run.

reports.review_kind: Independent read-only preliminary STRICT component source re-review

prior_own_findings_disposition.evidence: The installed argv0 Docker entry derives a canonical configuration-directory digest from its actual inherited DOCKER_CONFIG or HOME/.docker and a DOCKER_HOST-presence flag. These bounded nonsecret fields travel in ToolRequest. qualify_native refuses a caller with host override or a routing reference different from the Runtime before qualification probes or creation admission. The qualified receipt durably retains config digest, explicit context and observed engine. Grant returns the routing reference and execute rechecks it immediately before the owned official-CLI spawn. The namespace overlay does not replace DOCKER_CONFIG/HOME or credentials. Historical cleanup refuses a different configuration reference or host override before helpers, and checks recorded context transport and observed engine before destructive commands. Therefore the previous ordinary A-directory Runtime/B-directory shim scenario now refuses before create; equal context names no longer admit that mismatch.
prior_own_findings_disposition.qualification: Closure covers configuration-reference mismatch in the currently finite inherited-context profile. Directory digest and sampled engine checks do not establish atomic endpoint/configuration immutability or a security boundary.

prior_own_findings_disposition.evidence: DockerKill and DockerRemove are appended with exact container target, Unknown outcome and NotAttempted confirmation before their awaited helper calls. Their durable helper target now contains action, full container ID and engine digest. reserve_cleanup_helper validates the historical claim, persists this exact target and commits before spawn; its allowed safe characters and 256-byte bound accommodate these identities. If the five-second outer timeout drops the await after the daemon effect but before acknowledgement, the borrowed report keeps the in-flight typed action and HelperGuard reconciles its registered exact target to Unknown. Partial earlier actions survive. Later successful receipt and independent inspection/inventory only refine outcome/confirmation.
prior_own_findings_disposition.qualification: This is static producer/consumer closure. A Runtime crash may still interrupt observation persistence; its prior durable exact helper intent remains uncertain, not proof of successful cleanup.

verified_source_observations.evidence: Tool entry runs before operational argument parsing. Routing validation belongs to actual request/grant execution paths, not only fixture helper calls. Existing exact owner/cookie/native authority and post-qualification admission fencing remain. Managed-effect intent precedes grant/spawn; lost lifecycle acknowledgement remains Unknown. No arbitrary environment or credential payload is sent through IPC.

verified_source_observations.topic: Exact historical target and Task independence
verified_source_observations.evidence: Historical claims bind exact epoch/job/unit/version/scope/generation/cookie and both closed authority flags. Docker mutation requires qualified historical context/engine, full ID, all four Runtime/Project/Task/unit labels and registered operation/name. It reinspects the identity and stopped state before non-forced removal. Tool run/create forces unique names plus namespace/operation labels; admitted port and mount forms remain unit-local. No sibling/global prune, forced removal or shared network/volume deletion path was introduced.

verified_source_observations.topic: Bounded partial receipt and actual persistence
verified_source_observations.evidence: Each initial/final container, network and volume inventory is bounded to 32. Their union can require 128 remaining identities; Docker's normalization caps/deduplicates partial results at 128 and adds finite limited-coverage error on truncation. Cookie observation takes at most 896 identities, so append_docker fits the actual 1024 persisted remaining bound. Docker destructive actions are at most 64, giving at most 960 combined actions; exact targets fit 256 bytes. Cookie errors are deduplicated finite categories, Docker errors are finite categories, and the combined path fits the 32-error persistence bound. State insertion, quarantine and next cleanup deadline affect only the historical unit and do not change work, Task progress or accepted artifacts. Empty or incomplete Docker observations do not become complete-release claims.

The component document names its selected Docker 28/API 1.48-1.51 profile, managed run/create/filtered ps, local named Unix contexts, and refusals for relative roots/DOCKER_HOST/remote transport/raw Compose. It explicitly separates protocol selection from real-daemon/native acceptance, and names raw delegation/image anonymous-volume/shared-resource limitations. Configuration-reference hashing reads directory/path metadata, not configuration or authentication file contents. No license or README claim change is present in the reviewed diff.

controls_inspected_but_not_executed.purpose: Account-free built-binary argv0/real IPC path: same context name in different configuration references refuses before fixture probes/effects, host override refuses, matching reference admits forced labels and recorded operation/name.
Fixture kill/remove applies effect then delays command acknowledgement; verifies uncertain exact typed action, durable target, historical observation round-trip and live sibling authority.

Changing valid inventories exercise 128 Docker identities plus 896 cookie identities through the actual append/persistence/history path; partial normalization and canonical/absolute/nonsecret reference checks.

additional_proposed_causal_controls_not_: Exercise historical cleanup with a changed Runtime configuration root and unchanged context name; assert refusal before inventory/kill and unknown coverage, never mutation of a different engine.

Exercise a HOME-derived reference versus an explicit DOCKER_CONFIG canonical alias, and a symlink reference changed between request and grant execution; expected semantic equality should admit and changed reference should refuse before effect.

Exercise multiple registered containers where an earlier action completes and a later kill/remove applies then loses acknowledgement. Ensure completed and uncertain action records both survive and sibling IDs/resources remain unchanged.
Qualify actual supported Docker CLI/template/version/context behavior and native sandbox/auth/settings/hooks separately on both target OSes. Fixed fixture source is not evidence those controls pass.
limits: Only immutable git objects at source, baseline and approved contract plus this reviewer's own prior report were read. No dirty/later source, peer findings, aggregate review document, progress document or test log was inspected.

No builds/tests, real Docker/native Agents/accounts/authentication/configuration probes, network activity, process signals or host/repository changes were performed. Only this authorized private review report was written; no parent test claims are inherited.
